title: Dr. Gachet
medium: Etching and drypoint, enhanced with black ink on laid paper

image.credit: Cleveland Museum of Art, Dudley P. Allen Fund

highlight.text: The doctor was himself an amateur printmaker and gave Van Gogh a varnished copper plate, helping him print it on his own small hand press. For his first attempt, Van Gogh depicted Gachet seated in his garden smoking a pipe.

work.text: This portrait of Dr. Paul Gachet, made just two months before the artist’s death, is the only etching that Vincent van Gogh created.

moment.text: I hope he does some etchings of southern subjects, say six, since I can print them without cost at M. Gachet's, who is kind enough to print them for nothing if I do them.

source.author: Vincent van Gogh
source.title: Letter 642 to Theo van Gogh, Auvers-sur-Oise, 17 June 1890
source.publisher: The Complete Letters of Vincent van Gogh, via WebExhibits

moment.lead: Hoping Gauguin would join him in printmaking:

matters.text: He is a very nervous man himself and very queer in his behaviour; he has extended much friendliness to the artists of the new school, and he has helped them as much as was in his power.

source.author: Vincent van Gogh
source.title: Letter W22 to Wilhelmina van Gogh, Auvers-sur-Oise, 5 June 1890
